title: QUIZ - 19
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a proportion for an unknown term using cross-multiplication
questions.question: Solve for x: \( 2/7 = 6/x \)
questions.explanation: Cross-multiplying gives \(2 \times x = 7 \times 6\), so x = 42/2 = 21.
questions.hint: Cross-multiply the two ratios, then solve the resulting equation for x.

questions.learningObjective: Apply proportional reasoning to scale a recipe or mixture
questions.question: A recipe uses the ratio 5:5 for two ingredients. If the first ingredient amount is scaled up to 30, what should the second ingredient amount (x) be, keeping the same ratio?
questions.explanation: Since the ratio must stay 5:5, solve 5/5 = 30/x by cross-multiplying: \(x = (5 \times 30)/5 = 30\).
questions.hint: Set up a proportion and cross-multiply to keep the ratio constant.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether two ratios form a true proportion using cross products
questions.question: Is \( 3/9 = 6/7 \) a true proportion?

options.label: A
options.text: It cannot be determined without simplifying both fractions.

options.label: B
options.text: No, because the cross products are not equal.

options.label: C
options.text: Yes, because both fractions have the same numerator.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, because the cross products are equal.

questions.explanation: Cross-multiplying: \(3 \times 7 = 21\) and \(9 \times 6 = 54\). Since \(21 \neq 54\), the two ratios are not equal, so this is not a true proportion.
questions.hint: A proportion is true only when the cross products of the two ratios are equal.
